From 46b1063f91e5680eff2a6b9fe432f6aae3bef54e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2018 08:22:06 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915: Handle recursive shrinker for vma->last_active
 allocation

If we call into the shrinker for direct relcaim inside kmalloc, it will
retire the requests. If we retire the vma->last_active while processing a
new i915_vma_move_to_active() we can upset the delicate bookkeeping
required for the cache. After the possible invocation of the shrinker, we
need to double check the vma->last_active is still valid.

Fixes: 8b293eb53a7d ("drm/i915: Track the last-active inside the i915_vma")
Bugzilla: https://bugs.freedesktop.org/show_bug.cgi?id=105600#c39
Signed-off-by: Chris Wilson <chris@chris-wilson.co.uk>
Cc: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Tvrtko Ursulin <tvrtko.ursulin@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20180719072206.16015-1-chris@chris-wilson.co.uk

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_vma.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_vma.c
index ed4e0fb558f7..11d834f94220 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_vma.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_vma.c
@@ -942,6 +942,14 @@ static struct i915_gem_active *active_instance(struct i915_vma *vma, u64 idx)
 	}
 
 	active = kmalloc(sizeof(*active), GFP_KERNEL);
+
+	/* kmalloc may retire the vma->last_active request (thanks shrinker)! */
+	if (unlikely(!i915_gem_active_raw(&vma->last_active,
+					  &vma->vm->i915->drm.struct_mutex))) {
+		kfree(active);
+		goto out;
+	}
+
 	if (unlikely(!active))
 		return ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM);
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_vma.c`**
- Added a check after the `kmalloc` call to verify if `vma->last_active` is still valid. This is done using the function `i915_gem_active_raw()`.
- If `vma->last_active` is not valid (indicating that it may have been retired by the shrinker), the newly allocated `active` instance is freed using `kfree(active)`, and the function exits early with a goto statement.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification addresses a potential issue where calling the shrinker during memory allocation (`kmalloc`) could inadvertently retire the `vma->last_active` request. This could disrupt the bookkeeping necessary for managing the cache of active instances. By adding a validation check for `vma->last_active` after the allocation, the patch ensures that the integrity of the active instance management is maintained, preventing possible errors in the system's memory management.
